title: Risk factors for dental implant failure in vascularized bone flaps: a decade-long cohort study
html: This study aims to evaluate the survival of dental implants placed exclusively within vascularized osseous free flaps for oral cavity reconstruction and to identify key risk factors for implant failure. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 105 patients who received 358 dental implants within fibula, scapula, or deep circumflex iliac artery free flaps at a single institution over a 10-year period. The primary outcome was implant failure, defined as removal for any reason. Statistical analysis employed multivariate mixed-effects Cox regression models to account for patient-level clustering and confounding variables, including adjuvant radiotherapy, jaw location, donor site, and smoking status.
